title: Noise-Robust Quantum State Characterization for Remote State Preparation with Deep Learning
authors: Bo Tang, Zixuan Liao, Hao Li, Yilin Yang, Jiani Lei, Zengya Li, Jing Qiu, Zhaohui Dong, Zhengyang Mao, Yuanhua Li, Yuanlin Zheng, Xianfeng Chen
abstract: Quantum communication underpins secure information processing and scalable quantum networks. In particular, remote state preparation (RSP) enables efficient quantum state transfer, but accurately estimating target states under complex noise remains challenging. Here, we propose a Transformer-based Quantum State Characterizer (TQSC) model for noisy RSP experiments. Our model reconstructs experimentally prepared pure and mixed photonic polarization states from noisy measurements in complex scattering environments, while its attention patterns provide physically grounded insights into correlations among the measured observables. The method achieves a mean estimator-target fidelity exceeding 99.999% under complex scattering and dynamic Gaussian noise, while its robustness and generalization are further examined using Qiskit-simulated Bloch-ball states.Furthermore, in a practical MNIST image transmission task with held-out states, the decoded bit error rate is reduced from 50.34% to zero after TQSC post-processing. The TQSC model enables accurate tomographic characterization under dynamic noise and provides physically grounded post-hoc insights, holding promise for intelligent quantum information processing applications.
summary: This paper introduces a Transformer-based Quantum State Characterizer (TQSC) to overcome the difficulty of accurately characterizing quantum states during noisy Remote State Preparation. By treating measurement data as a sequence, the model reconstructs the true quantum state with extremely high fidelity, even in the presence of complex scattering and dynamic noise. This work offers a robust, data-driven tool for practical quantum information processing applications.
main_problem: The core challenge is accurately estimating target quantum states during Remote State Preparation (RSP) when the measurements are corrupted by complex, dynamic noise.
main_result: The proposed TQSC model achieved an extremely high mean estimator-target fidelity (>99.999%) under complex noise and successfully reduced the bit error rate to zero in a practical MNIST image transmission task.
method: The authors developed a Transformer-based Quantum State Characterizer (TQSC) model that treats noisy measurement outcomes as sequential data to reconstruct the underlying quantum density matrix.
model_or_system: The system involves photonic polarization states generated via an SPDC source in a Sagnac interferometer setup. The TQSC model uses a Transformer Encoder architecture to map noisy measurement data back to the predicted quantum state, incorporating physical constraints.
key_observables: Mean estimator-target fidelity, bit error rate (BER), density matrices ($ho$), and Transformer attention patterns.
important_parameters: Complex scattering environments, dynamic Gaussian noise ($\sigma=1 	ext{ V}$), and the fidelity threshold of 99.999%.
main_assumptions: The method assumes that the noise can be modeled and inverted using a data-driven, attention-based neural network structure, moving beyond traditional black-box approaches.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the experimental setup (Sagnac loop, RSP) and the data processing pipeline involving the Transformer. Other figures detail the performance metrics under noise and the MNIST image transmission results.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem of noisy RSP, details the TQSC model architecture (Transformer-based inverse channel mapping), validates its performance using fidelity metrics under controlled noise, and demonstrates its utility in a practical image transmission task.
why_interesting: It provides a powerful, data-driven framework for quantum state tomography and characterization that explicitly handles complex, realistic noise sources, which is crucial for advancing quantum networking and communication protocols.
